title: Long-horizon quantization calibration harness: throughput & tail-latency scan (FP8/INT8, batching interactions)
creator: Evelyn Chen
description: Create a repeatable benchmarking harness and experimental matrix that validates throughput and tail-latency behavior for FP8 and INT8 quantized variants on long-context workloads. Focus on how batching policies (static vs adaptive), KV-cache warmup/eviction behavior, and calibration choices (per-layer vs per-channel, dataset size, symmetric/asymmetric) interact to affect p50/p95/p99 latency, overall token throughput, and downstream accuracy regressions for representative prompt sets. Deliverables: reproducible scripts, calibrated profiles, dashboards, a short runbook with recommended default calibration presets for hosted and dedicated runtimes.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Harness can run nightly matrix of: precisions [FP8, INT8], calibration modes [per-layer, per-channel], batch sizes [1,2,4,8,16,32], context lengths [2048,8192,32768], KV-warmup states [cold,20%,50%,100%].
2) For each run we capture: p50/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/sec, memory usage, KV-cache hit rate, and accuracy metrics (perplexity delta on eval set + top-1 token error).
3) Results are uploaded to perf-dashboard (link in comments) and a short summary with recommended default profiles for hosted vs dedicated is posted to the runtime-1.22 release notes.
4) Regressions > 5% throughput or > 15% p99 increase compared to FP16 baseline are flagged automatically and create a follow-up ticket.
reproduction_steps:
1) Checkout repo: github.com/redwood-inference/perf/quant-harness (PR #789).
2) Activate conda env: conda activate ri-perf && pip install -r requirements.txt.
3) Provision test cluster: ./scripts/provision_test_cluster --flavor=dedicated-small --gpus=4.
4) Run orchestrator: python run_matrix.py --matrix config/matrix-default.yaml --outdir /mnt/results/ENG-52345.
5) Upload results: ./scripts/upload_results --path /mnt/results/ENG-52345 --dashboard perf/quant/long-horizon.
6) Check dashboards and the artifacts folder for calibration checkpoints and logs.
comments: 2026-02-25 - Evelyn Chen: Created ticket. Initial scope discussed with runtime team. Goal is to produce conservative default calibration profiles usable by hosted API and a set of guardrails for Dedicated customers. Blocking question: do we validate against both in-distribution eval and a small adversarial prompt set? Recommendation: yes, both.

2026-03-01 - Miguel Torres: Prototype harness landed in feature branch. Key files: run_matrix.py, config/matrix-longcontext.yaml. Early microbenchmarks show FP8 throughput gains of 1.8x at batch=16 for seq=2048 but p99 worsens by ~20% when KV warmup is cold. Recording artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/ENG-52345/initial.

2026-03-03 - Lina Gomez: Ran accuracy sweep with calibration dataset sizes [1k,5k,20k]. Observations: INT8 per-channel with 5k samples keeps perplexity delta <1.5% vs FP16 on in-distribution eval; FP8 shows small distributional bias in a small subset of tokens for the adversarial set. See PR #794 for calibration tooling changes.

2026-03-05 - Priya Shah: KV-cache experiment: with adaptive batching enabled, we saw improved tokens/sec for mixed small/large sequences but p99 tail increased when KV eviction occurred mid-session. Hypothesis: cache thrashing + batch coalescing increases serialization events on the runtime. Need trace-level logs to confirm.

2026-03-07 - Miguel Torres: Added trace hooks and a micro-tracing dashboard. Re-ran batch=8/16 matrix with cold vs 100% warm KV. Results: FP8 p99 at seq=32768, batch=16, cold KV = 1.9s token latency (vs FP16 baseline 1.6s) and throughput -22% compared to FP16. With KV warm=100% throughput gap narrows to -6% and p99 gap to +8%.

2026-03-09 - Ravi Singh: Noted a calibration config that improved FP8 tail: switching to per-channel symmetric quant + bias-correction reduced p99 by ~12% at the cost of ~3% throughput. Adding this as a candidate default for Dedicated.
notes: We must be careful when promoting FP8 defaults for hosted API. Early data suggests FP8 gives best cost/throughput for warm, predictable workloads with high batching, but fragile for cold-start or highly mixed sequence-length traffic. INT8 per-channel is a safer middle ground for heterogeneous traffic. The runbook will reflect this nuance.
next_steps: Stabilize nightly runs and wire regression alerting to perf-alerts (owner: Miguel).

Create a short runtime config proposal that exposes two calibration presets: hosted-robust (INT8 per-channel, conservative bias-correction) and dedicated-aggressive (FP8 per-channel symmetric with bias-correction).
Add multi-tenant headroom tests (simulate 10 tenants with varied sequence distributions) to detect cross-tenant KV eviction effects.
Draft runtime-1.22 release note paragraph and attach recommended default profiles and a one-page runbook.
If regressions flagged, create follow-up triage ticket with traces and calibration artifact links.
